newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: INDUSTRIAL REFORMS AID DECLINE OF UNIONISM, SAYS REITH
Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith says his reforms are contributing to the fall of union membership in Australia.
The latest Bureau of Statistics' figures show union membership has declined by one third in the past 10 years.
Mr Reith says a lot of people are only just starting to realise that under the new law if they give two weeks notice they can get out of a union.
The ABS survey says the unionised percentage of all employees has been dropping since August 1986, from 46 per cent to 31 per cent last year.
In its analysis the bureau attributes the decline to the change in full-time and part-time working patterns.
The ACTU won't comment on the figures until it examines the survey.
KENNETT CONCEDES, BUT SAYS LIBS WILL WIN SEAT BACK
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, has blamed preferences from the anti-immigration and gun lobbies, for the Liberal Party's defeat in the West Gippsland by-election.
After more counting today, Mr Kennett admits only a miracle can stop Independent, Susan Davies, from taking the previously safe Government seat.
He says it's "food for thought" that Ms Davies received preferences from the Australian Reform Party.
Mr Kennett says the result won't lead to change in the Government's policies, and predicts the Liberals will regain the seat at the next election.
IMMIGRATION STUDY EXPECTED TO EXPLODE MYTHS
A study by the Immigration Department shows almost a quarter of Australia's resident population was born overseas, over half of them in Europe.
It also shows the importance of tourism as a foreign exchange earner for Australia, bringing in around A$14 billion in 1995-96.
Federal Immigration Minister Phillip Ruddock says he hopes the study will combat misinformation which has peppered the debate on race and immigration.
The study looks at the make-up of immigration, including a state-by-state analysis and the impact on the labour market.
Mr Ruddock is beginning a round of consultations on next year's immigration program.
He says he expects to talk to about two-thousand individuals and organisations.
BOND "SHOWS REMORSE" FOR BELL RESOURCES FRAUD
A Supreme Court judge in Perth has been told that an admission by former tycoon Alan Bond of his part in the nation's biggest case of corporate fraud is a sign of his remorse.
Justice Michael Murray has been hearing sentencing submissions following Bond's plea of guilty to two charges of failing to act honestly as a company director.
The charges relate to the transfer in the late 1980s of more than A$1 billion from the company Bell Resources to Bond Corporation.
Today, Bond's Defence Counsel said his client had saved the community time and expense by pleading guilty and giving up appeals against his conviction and sentence for an art fraud offence.
Bond is serving a three-year jail term for that conviction.
PILOT WALKS AWAY FROM PLANE CRASH IN PERTH
A water bombing plane has crashed into a house in the Perth suburb of Maddington, while attending a bushfire.
The Dromadier aircraft clipped one house in Conifer Street, and crashed into another causing extensive damage.
A spokesman from the Bushfires Board says the pilot walked away from the crash, and is believed to be uninjured.
Emergency workers are attempting to find out whether the house was occupied.
The light aircraft was dropping water on a fire near the Tonkin Highway.
It's understood power lines in the area are down, and roads in the area are closed.
EXERCISE PERIOD COULD PUT BRYANT IN DANGER
Prison officers say Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant could be put in danger by a decision to allow him to mix with other prisoners.
Tasmania's Correctional Officers Association says there are not enough staff at Risdon prison to ensure Bryant's safety during his one-hour exercise period.

The deputy head of the Tasmania's Department of Correctional Services Department, Denby Richards, says the exercise period is normal treatment for prisoners like Bryant and is done under appropriate controls.
Mr Richard's says Bryant is allowed only a very limited amount of interaction with other prisoners.
Bryant is let out of his solitary cell for one hour each day, to exercise with up to eight other inmates in the prison yard.
SHARK ATTACKS KAYAKER ON PARRAMATTA RIVER
A Sydney woman who was paddling in her kayak this morning is counting her blessings after a shark knocked her out of the boat, but then decided to move away.
Police say the woman, who is in her mid-fifties, was sculling on the Parramatta River at around six o'clock when the shark knocked her from the boat.
The shark did not follow up the attack, allowing the woman to climb back into the kayak and paddle to shore.
She has minor bruising and is recovering from shock.
Teeth marks were found on her boat.
